title: Vectorize layernorm and the swiglu erf
description: At L=512 the two layernorms (1.45 ms each, double scalar loops) and the swiglu (3 ms, a libm erff per element over [512 x 2624]) are ~165 ms of the 680 ms encoder. Spell the layernorm reductions out in lanes; give swiglu a branch-free erf polynomial the compiler vectorizes, checked against libm erff. lla_gelu stays on libm erff: it only runs on the scorer's marker rows and doubles as the reference.
acceptance_criteria: goldens unchanged; swiglu vs gelu(libm)*gate within 1e-6 rel; layer at L=512 loses >= 3 ms
close_reason: layernorm 1.45->0.61 ms, swiglu 3.0->3.2 ms with tail-accurate erfc (A&S was 2.4 ms but 2e-6 off in the tail); 512 tokens 742->529 ms, 55 tokens 129->96

title: Reuse one per-forward workspace instead of per-layer allocations
description: Every encoder layer allocates ~40 MB of fresh arena memory (qkv, q/k/v heads, scores, ctx, wi, swiglu, residuals); ffi/alloc zeroes and fresh pages fault in, ~7 ms per layer, ~190 ms of ~950 at L=512 and ~15% at L=55. Allocate the intermediates once per forward (sized by row count so batching composes) and let the kernels overwrite them; every op already writes every element of its output.
acceptance_criteria: goldens unchanged; forward at L=512 drops by >=150 ms; memory per forward bounded by one workspace
close_reason: 512-token question 857->742 ms (-115 ms; the >=150 in the acceptance was an overestimate: the workspace itself still faults in ~50 MB once per call); 55 tokens 136->129. Goldens unchanged.

title: Masked softmax: band-limit sliding layers, vectorizable expf
description: After the sgemm swap, attention at L=512 is 11.5 ms per full layer of which the two gemms are 1.4 ms: lla_masked_softmax makes 16x512x512 scalar expf calls and three passes per head. Sliding layers (18 of 28) still score and scan all 512 keys per query for a 129-wide band. Per forward at 512 that is ~210 ms of ~950. Restrict sliding layers to the band (blocked QK^T/PV over [i-w, i+w]) and make the exp loop vectorizable (polynomial expf, ~2 ulp, verified against libm in a test).
acceptance_criteria: goldens unchanged at 1e-4; expf test max rel err < 5e-7 over [-88, 0]; attention full < 5 ms, sliding < 2 ms per layer at L=512
close_reason: full 11.0->6.9 ms, sliding 7.3->3.7 ms per layer at L=512; 512-token question 943->857 ms; expf within 2e-6 rel of libm

title: Attention via per-head sgemm; band-limit sliding layers
description: lla_attention: QK^T and PV as cblas_sgemm per head (split-qkv already lays each head out as a contiguous [L x hd] block). On sliding layers only the |i-j|<=window band is needed; skip the rest. Keep lla_scores/lla_weighted_sum callable for the kernel tests.
acceptance_criteria: tensors_test layer goldens pass (1e-4 abs, 5e-5 rel last layer); readme/presets answers unchanged; scale bench: 512 tokens under 1.2 s, ~linear in L
close_reason: 512 tokens 4.8 s -> 996 ms, linear in L; suite green at 1e-4; byte-identity claim retired (boundary value 0.314250x). Band-limiting sliding layers skipped: attention is now ~0.04 s of ~1 s at L=512, ~0.19 s of ~2 s at 1024, so the band would save well under 0.1 s.

title: Latency: attention kernel, batched encoder, constrained decoding
description: One noul question takes 182 ms at 55 tokens and 4.8 s at 512 tokens. The only O(L^2) term is attention, and lla_scores / the PV loop in native/laya_kernels.c are scalar loops with a double accumulator while every other matmul goes through cblas_sgemm. Per-head sgemm does the same work ~90x faster (0.04 s vs 3.9 s at L=512 over 30 layers). After that the encoder is weight-GEMM bound and batching a call's questions pays. Then port GLiNER2's constrained multi-task decoder (torch-free) as a workflow/API extension so answers across questions are consistent.

title: Linux release binary: jolt build's static relink fails (PIE) — v0.1.0 shipped mac only
description: The release workflow's x86_64-linux job fails at jolt build's relink of the launcher with our static kernel archive: libkernel.a(foreign.o) relocation R_X86_64_32 against S_tc_mutex cannot be used when making a PIE object (Ubuntu gcc defaults to PIE; jolt's bundled Chez kernel is not PIC). Same on jolt 0.8.9 and 0.8.10; mac is fine. v0.1.0 therefore has only the aarch64-macos asset. Filed upstream as jolt-lang/jolt#1060 (suggested: -no-pie on the linux relink). Until it lands: either wait, or drop :static on linux and ship liblaya_kernels.so beside the binary (the launcher then needs it on the host's library path).
acceptance_criteria: release workflow green on both targets; the linux tarball self-tests

title: laya.patterns: von's composable decision patterns, plus escalation to a thinking model
description: Port von.patterns (github.com/wfzyx/von src/von/patterns.py) over system-one: confidence-gate (split answers into automatic / escalate at a confidence threshold; noul confidence = |p - 0.5| * 2), route (a choice question dispatched to a handler map with a min confidence and a default), composite-score (weighted mean of normalised score/noul answers in [0, 1] with a breakdown), two-stage-choice (category then option for taxonomies past ~20 options, combined confidence = product). Then the pattern the benchmark shows matters: escalate the cases below the gate to a generative model with thinking through an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint (llama-server with MiniCPM5-2B: 97.2% on authored144 at ~3 s/case on Metal, versus laya's 61% at 117 ms and von's 76% at 160 ms; a gate at 0.5 on laya's top-2 margin sends 92/144 up and lands at 88.9%). Constraints (laya.constraints) apply after the gate, over the merged answers.
acceptance_criteria: unit tests for each pattern on a fake agent; escalation tested against a stub HTTP endpoint (grammar-constrained answer, thinking on/off); workflow files can declare a pattern; the HTTP API exposes confidence_gate and escalation options; README section

title: von-1.0 as a checkpoint: zero-shot NLI decisions on the ModernBERT-large encoder
description: wfzyx/von-1.0 (github.com/wfzyx/von, Apache-2.0) is tasksource/ModernBERT-large-nli fine-tuned with CE+Brier on ANLI/WANLI/MNLI/SNLI: the same ModernBERT-large encoder laya-jolt already runs (28 layers, d=1024, rope 160k/10k, window 64), plus ModernBertForSequenceClassification's head (mean pooling over the attention mask of final_norm -> head.dense 1024x1024 no bias -> erf GELU -> LayerNorm no bias -> classifier 3x1024 + bias; entailment = logit 0), T = 1.0367 from calibration.json. Every option becomes one pair sequence [CLS] state [SEP] hypothesis [SEP] (truncation longest_first at 512), the entailment logits over a question's options are softmaxed. Hypotheses: choice = instructions + ' ' + (description or option); score = instructions + ' Level i: ' + description; noul = instructions + ' ' + (criteria true or 'Condition holds true.') vs (criteria false or 'Condition is false or not satisfied.'). On authored144 it scores 76.4% against laya english 61.1% / typed-decisions 66.7% (bench/README.md), at ~160 ms/case in torch on CPU. Weights are at ~/src/models/von-1.0 (model.safetensors: model.* encoder tensors, head.*, classifier.*). Answer shapes follow von's own (choice: confidence = p1 - p2 rounded to 3; score: score rounded to 2; noul: just noul), so von's Python is the parity oracle.
design: Encoder shared with laya (rename model.* -> encoder.* at prepare); a new head fn in laya.model (mean-pool + dense + gelu + norm + classifier); a pair sequence builder; system-one dispatch on (:engine cfg): :laya (marker head) or :nli (per-option pairs batched through forward-batch's encoder path). The router treats it as a fourth checkpoint name (von), explicit only.
acceptance_criteria: jolt prepare --model von converts it into data/von; model: "von" routes to it; decisions identical and probabilities within 1e-3 of von's BertaBackend on authored144 (dump golden/von/ from it); bench/authored144.clj --model von reports its accuracy and ms/case; README documents the engine and its answer shape

title: MiniCPM5-2B for the accuracy gap: measure before porting
description: The hosted Jev (jev-1.13.0) is a generative model with a 240-token scaffold and scores 60/64 on the benchmark where the laya checkpoint scores 24/64. openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B-GGUF is a 2.5B decoder-only LlamaForCausalLM (42 layers, 16 q heads / 2 kv heads, 131k context, thinking mode, Apache-2.0; Q4_K_M 1.56 GB, Q8_0 2.68 GB, F16 5.04 GB). Whether it closes the gap is an empirical question: run it through llama.cpp on the 64 cases with the same typed-question prompt and a constrained answer (logit scoring of the option tokens, no free generation) and compare accuracy and latency against laya and Jev before deciding on a jolt port (GGUF loader, dequant, llama decoder with GQA/RMSNorm/SwiGLU, KV cache).
acceptance_criteria: a table: accuracy on the 64 cases and ms per case for laya, MiniCPM5-2B Q8_0 and F16 (thinking off, option-logit scoring), with a go/no-go on the port
close_reason: measured: see bench/README.md. MiniCPM5-2B thinking 97.2% at 3 s/case Metal, 10 s CPU; direct 73.6%; von-1.0 76.4%; laya 61-67%. A jolt decoder port is not the next step: escalation to llama-server (laya-jolt-5m1) and the von head (laya-jolt-ct5) are.

title: Restore the reduce form of lowest-ranked-pair (jolt 0.8.10 fixes the nil-init reduce miscompile)
description: jolt 0.8.10 (released 2026-09-19) types a built reduce accumulator as the fixpoint of init and the closure's return, so the nil-init reduce that 0.8.9 folded wrong now compiles right (verified: the changelog's one-liner answers 1 in a release build). Put lowest-ranked-pair back as a reduce, update the docstring, README 'As a binary' and release.yml comments to say which version had the bug, and prove it with jolt binary's self-test.
acceptance_criteria: tokenizer tests green; ./laya-server --self-test green on a fresh jolt build
close_reason: reduce form restored; jolt binary self-test green on 0.8.10

title: Multithread the per-row C kernels (attention, swiglu, layernorm)
description: At 512 tokens a layer spends 3-6 ms in attention (16 heads, each two sgemms + a masked softmax, run one after another from Clojure), 2.4 ms in swiglu and 0.5 ms in layernorm, all on one core, while the four big gemms (7 ms) are already multi-core through Accelerate. Move the head loop into the kernel library (lla_attention, sgemm reached through a function pointer from jolt.ffi/find-symbol so the library stays BLAS-free at link time) and run heads x query blocks, swiglu rows and layernorm rows on a persistent pthread pool with per-thread S/P scratch. Thread count: LAYA_THREADS / lla_set_threads, default the online cores.
design: Pool: N-1 workers + the caller, atomic task counter, one job at a time (inference is serialized behind the server lock). Scratch owned by the pool, grown on demand. Kernels write disjoint rows/columns per task so no locking inside a job. The Clojure attention! keeps its signature; S/P in the workspace go away.
acceptance_criteria: attention/swiglu/layernorm tests pass unchanged with threads=1 and threads=N (bit-identical across thread counts: the same per-row arithmetic runs, only the schedule changes); golden suite green; 512-token single row under 400 ms (from 529); jolt binary self-test green
close_reason: pool + lla_attention; bit-identical across thread counts; 512-token row 516->347 ms, email 2.3->1.5 s; suite and binary self-test green

title: Constrained multi-question decoding (port of gliner2.classification)
description: Port gliner2/classification/{constraints,candidates}.py and decoding/ (torch-free): constraint AST as EDN (implies, iff, excludes, not, all-of, any-of, exactly-one-of, at-least/at-most/exactly, at-level/min-level/max-level/between-level, any-selected), Kleene 3-valued evaluation, exact DFS with branch-and-bound, beam fallback, relax -> min-violations -> raise ladder. choice <-> single, score <-> ordinal, a set of nouls <-> multi. Consumes the per-question probability vectors system-one already computes. Workflows declare constraints; the API accepts them; answers without constraints stay byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria: unit tests for the evaluator and decoders incl. exact-vs-brute-force; email workflow with spam => not needs_reply; feasible/violations reported in the answer
close_reason: laya.constraints + wiring; 14 unit tests incl. brute-force parity; suite 115 tests green

title: Batch a call's questions through the encoder
description: system-one runs forward-row once per question; each pass re-reads 1.7 GB of weights. Stack the B rows into one [B*L x d] stream per layer so weights are read once, with per-row attention and masks. Rows have different L; pad to the max with the attention mask, or group by length.
acceptance_criteria: answers byte-identical to the unbatched path on the goldens; demo (4 questions) and email (5) measurably faster than 1x per question
close_reason: demo 526->364 ms, triage 516->422, email 2490->2377; padded batch == row forwards == torch golden batch

title: Benchmark gliner2.5 on the 64-case set before deciding on a port
description: pip install gliner2[local]; classify_text with the same labels/instructions on the 64 cases from the Jev comparison. Decides whether a DeBERTa-v3 + Unigram tokenizer port to jolt is worth it (~1500 lines; one forward pass for all questions, 74M/194M params).
notes: authored144 (bench/) is now the fixed benchmark; the 64-case set from the other session is not on this machine. gliner2.5 (DeBERTa-v3 NLI-style) is likely in von's range; run it through bench/data when the case set is available.
